blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA?
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA?
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: STELARA is a medicine that affects your immune system. STELARA can increase your risk of having serious side effects, including:
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA?
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Serious infections. STELARA may lower the ability of your immune system to fight infections and may increase your risk of infections. Some people have serious infections during treatment with STELARA, including tuberculosis (TB), and infections caused by bacteria, fungi, or viruses. Some people have to be hospitalized for treatment of their infection.
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA?
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: o Your healthcare provider should check you for TB before starting STELARA.
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA?
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: o If your healthcare provider feels that you are at risk for TB, you may be treated with medicine for TB before you begin treatment with STELARA and during treatment with STELARA.
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA?
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: o Your healthcare provider should watch you closely for signs and symptoms of TB while you are being treated with STELARA.
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA?
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: You should not start STELARA if you have any kind of infection unless your healthcare provider says it is okay. Before starting STELARA, tell your healthcare provider if you:
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA?
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: o think you have an infection or have symptoms of an infection such as:
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA?
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  fever, sweat, or chills
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA?
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  muscle aches
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA?
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  cough
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA?
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  weight loss
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA?
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  warm, red, or painful skin or sores on your body
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA?
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  diarrhea or stomach pain
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA?
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  shortness of breath
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA?
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  blood in phlegm
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA?
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  burning when you urinate or urinate more often than normal
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA?
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  feel very tired
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA?
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: o are being treated for an infection or have any open cuts.
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA?
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: o get a lot of infections or have infections that keep coming back.
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA?
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: o have TB or have been in close contact with someone with TB.
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA?
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: After starting STELARA, call your healthcare provider right away if you get any symptoms of an infection (see above). These may be signs of infections such as chest infections, or skin infections or shingles that could have serious complications. STELARA can make you more likely to get infections or make an infection that you have worse.
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA?
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  People who have a genetic problem where the body does not make any of the proteins interleukin 12 (IL-12) and interleukin 23 (IL-23) are at a higher risk for certain serious infections. These infections can spread throughout the body and cause death. People who take STELARA may also be more likely to get these infections.
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA?
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Cancers. STELARA may decrease the activity of your immune system and increase your risk for certain types of cancers. Tell your healthcare provider if you have ever had any type of cancer. Some people who are receiving STELARA and have risk factors for skin cancer have developed certain types of skin cancers. During your treatment with STELARA, tell your healthcare provider if you develop any new skin growths.
section_path: What is the most important information I should know about STELARA?
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: What is STELARA?
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: STELARA is a prescription medicine used to treat:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  adults and children 6 years of age and older with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis who may benefit from taking injections or pills (systemic therapy) or phototherapy (treatment using ultraviolet light alone or with pills).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  adults and children 6 years of age and older with active psoriatic arthritis.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  adults and children 2 years of age and older with moderately to severely active Crohn's disease.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  adults and children 2 years of age and older with moderately to severely active ulcerative colitis.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: It is not known if STELARA is safe and effective in children less than 2 years of age with Crohn's disease, in children less than 2 years of age with ulcerative colitis or in children less than 6 years of age with plaque psoriasis or psoriatic arthritis.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Who should not use STELARA?
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Do not use STELARA if you are allergic to any ustekinumab product or any of the ingredients in STELARA. See the end of this Medication Guide for a complete list of ingredients in STELARA.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Before you use or receive STELARA, tell your healthcare provider about all of your medical conditions, including if you:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  have any of the conditions or symptoms listed in the section "What is the most important information I should know about STELARA?"
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  ever had an allergic reaction to STELARA. Ask your healthcare provider if you are not sure.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  are allergic to latex. The needle cover on the prefilled syringe contains latex.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  have recently received or are scheduled to receive an immunization (vaccine). People who are being treated with STELARA should avoid receiving live vaccines. Tell your healthcare provider if anyone in your house needs a live
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: page_footer
blocks.text: Reference ID: 5860727
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: vaccine. The viruses used in some types of live vaccines can spread to people with a weakened immune system, and can cause serious problems. You should avoid receiving the BCG vaccine during the 1 year before receiving STELARA or 1 year after you stop receiving STELARA.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  have any new or changing lesions within psoriasis areas or on normal skin.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  are receiving or have received allergy shots, especially for serious allergic reactions. Allergy shots may not work as well for you during treatment with STELARA. STELARA may also increase your risk of having an allergic reaction to an allergy shot.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  receive or have received phototherapy for your psoriasis.

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Important Information You Need to Know Before Injecting STELARA:
section_path: Important Information You Need to Know Before Injecting STELARA:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  For subcutaneous use only (inject directly under the skin).
section_path: Important Information You Need to Know Before Injecting STELARA:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Before you start, check the carton to make sure that the number of vials and strength is correct. You will have either 45 mg or 90 mg as prescribed by the healthcare provider.
section_path: Important Information You Need to Know Before Injecting STELARA:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: o If the dose is 45 mg or less, you will receive one 45 mg vial.
section_path: Important Information You Need to Know Before Injecting STELARA:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: o If the dose is more than 45 mg, you will receive two 45 mg vials and you will need to give two injections, one right after the other.
section_path: Important Information You Need to Know Before Injecting STELARA:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text: o Make sure you know the proper amount (volume) to remove from the vial (s) and type of syringe(s) needed for dosing. If you do not know the amount or type of syringe(s) needed, contact your healthcare provider for further instructions.
section_path: Important Information You Need to Know Before Injecting STELARA:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Check the expiration date on the vial and carton. If the expiration date has passed, do not use it. If the expiration date has passed, call the healthcare provider or pharmacist, or call 1-800-526-7736 for help.
section_path: Important Information You Need to Know Before Injecting STELARA:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Check the vial for any particles or discoloration. The liquid in the vial should look clear and colorless to light yellow with a few small clear or white particles.
section_path: Important Information You Need to Know Before Injecting STELARA:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Do not use if it is frozen, discolored, cloudy or has large particles. Get a new vial.
section_path: Important Information You Need to Know Before Injecting STELARA:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Do not shake the vial at any time. Shaking the vial may damage the STELARA medicine. If the vial has been shaken, do not use it. Get a new vial.
section_path: Important Information You Need to Know Before Injecting STELARA:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Do not use a STELARA vial more than 1 time, even if there is medicine left in the vial. After the rubber stopper is punctured, STELARA can become contaminated by harmful bacteria which could cause an infection if re-used. Therefore, throw away any unused STELARA after you give the injection.
section_path: Important Information You Need to Know Before Injecting STELARA:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Safely throw away (dispose of) STELARA vials, needles, and syringes after use. See "Step 6: Disposing of needles, syringes, and vials. "
section_path: Important Information You Need to Know Before Injecting STELARA:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Do not re-use syringes or needles.
section_path: Important Information You Need to Know Before Injecting STELARA:
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  To avoid needle-stick injuries, do not recap needles.
section_path: Important Information You Need to Know Before Injecting STELARA:

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Step 1: Preparing the injection
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Choose a well-lit, clean, flat work surface.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Wash your hands well with soap and warm water.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Step 2: Preparing the injection site
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Choose an injection site around the stomach area (abdomen), buttocks, and upper legs (thighs).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  If a caregiver is giving the injection, the outer area of the upper arms may also be used. (See Figure B)
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Use a different injection site for each injection. Do not give an injection in an area of the skin that is tender, bruised, red or hard.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Clean the skin with an antiseptic wipe where you plan to give the injection.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Do not touch this area again before giving the injection. Let the skin dry before injecting.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Do not fan or blow on the clean area.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.text: Step 3: Preparing the vial
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Remove the cap from the top of the vial. Throw away the cap but do not remove the rubber stopper. (See Figure C)
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Figure C
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Clean the rubber stopper with an antiseptic wipe. (See Figure D)
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Figure D
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Do not touch the rubber stopper after you clean it.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Put the vial on a flat surface.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: page_footer
blocks.text: Reference ID: 5860727

blocks.label: section_header
blocks.text: Step 4: Preparing the syringe
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Pick up the syringe with the needle attached.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Remove the cap that covers the needle. (See Figure E)
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Throw the needle cap away. Do not touch the needle or allow the needle to touch anything.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Pull back on the syringe plunger with your other hand.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Figure E
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Carefully pull back on the plunger to the line that matches the dose prescribed by the healthcare provider.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Hold the vial between your thumb and index (pointer) finger.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Use your other hand to push the syringe needle through the center of the rubber stopper. (See Figure F)
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Figure F
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Push down on the plunger until all of the air has gone from the syringe into the vial.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Turn the vial and the syringe upside down. (See Figure G)
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Hold the STELARA vial with 1 hand.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  It is important that the needle is always in the liquid in order to prevent air bubbles forming in the syringe.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: page_footer
blocks.text: Reference ID: 5860727
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Fill the syringe until the black tip of the plunger lines up with the mark that matches the prescribed dose.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Figure G
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Do not remove the needle from the vial. Hold the syringe with the needle pointing up to see if it has any air bubbles inside.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  If there are air bubbles, gently tap the side of the syringe until the air bubbles rise to the top. (See Figure H)
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Slowly press the plunger up until all of the air bubbles are out of the syringe (but none of the liquid is out).
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Remove the syringe from the vial. Do not lay the syringe down or allow the needle to touch anything.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Figure H
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Step 5: Injecting STELARA
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: page_footer
blocks.text: Reference ID: 5860727
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Hold the barrel of the syringe in 1 hand, between the thumb and index fingers.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Do not pull back on the plunger at any time.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Use the other hand to gently pinch the cleaned area of skin. Hold firmly.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Use a quick, dart-like motion to insert the needle into the pinched skin at about a 45degree angle. (See Figure I)
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Figure I
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  Push the plunger with your thumb as far as it will go to inject all of the liquid. Push it slowly and evenly, keeping the skin gently pinched.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  When the syringe is empty, pull the needle out of the skin and then let go of the skin. (See Figure J)
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: Figure J
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: list_item
blocks.text:  When the needle is pulled out of the skin, there may be a little bleeding at the injection site. This is normal. You can press a cotton ball or gauze pad to the injection site if needed. Do not rub the injection site. You may cover the injection site with a small adhesive bandage, if necessary.
blocks.speaker: label

blocks.label: text
blocks.text: If the dose is more than 45 mg, you will receive two 45 mg vials and you will need to give a second injection right after the first. Repeat Steps 1 to 5 using a new syringe. Choose a different site for the second injection.
